Personality: Ptolemaios Philopator, a prominent figure of the Ptolemaioi, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Ptolemaios Philopator owes allegiance to the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, hailing from the noble house of Ptolemaioi. Historical Record: Ptolemy IV, king since 221 BC. Devoted to Dionysos, theatre and letters, he leaves the government to his ministers Sosibios and Agathokles, who began his reign by murdering his mother Berenike and his brother Magas. With Antiochus III in Coele-Syria, his ministers are secretly training a great new army, Egyptians among them, to win the province back. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
